You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About the Role

As an Implementation Project Manager at 3E, you’ll lead larger, more complex customer implementations where successful delivery requires multiple products, technical contributors, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders to operate against one coordinated plan.

You’ll be accountable for turning the customer’s scope of work into an executable implementation strategy and for determining whether the overall project succeeds—on time, within scope, adopted, and connected to a clear customer outcome. You’ll establish success and acceptance criteria, own the integrated project plan, manage risk and change, coordinate specialists and technical teams, and give both customers and 3E leadership a clear, data-backed view of project health.

You’ll understand the technical delivery deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify dependencies, connect customer needs with the right specialists, and engage credibly with Product and Engineering. You won’t need to personally execute every configuration, migration, or integration; your role is to ensure those pieces come together into a successful customer outcome.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead complex new-logo, cross-sell, and Value Realization implementations from internal handoff through customer acceptance and formal close.

  • Translate complex scopes of work into an integrated delivery strategy covering products, workstreams, milestones, resources, dependencies, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria.

  • Lead technical discovery and pre-integration planning with customers, CX technical specialists, and relevant internal teams.

  • Own the master implementation plan and coordinate implementation specialists, Product, Engineering, Data, Cloud, technical consultants, external partners, and customer resources.

  • Establish measurable success and acceptance criteria at kickoff and maintain accountability for those outcomes throughout delivery.

  • Lead customer project governance, including senior stakeholder and sponsor communications.

  • Maintain the milestone tracker and conduct phase-gate reviews, giving a clear assessment of whether projects are on track, at risk, or behind and establishing mitigation plans when required.

  • Identify cross-workstream dependencies and risks early and determine their impact on the critical path.

  • Lead complex, multi-product delivery by managing scope and change control, coordinating custom development through launch, maintaining a unified customer plan across teams, and providing leadership with clear, data-backed reporting on project health, risk, timelines, value, and adoption.

  • Build and maintain dashboards or reporting tools that make project status and risks visible without relying solely on status meetings.

  • Lead customer escalations diplomatically while maintaining accountability for customer commitments, decisions, resources, data readiness, and signoffs.

  • Partner with Commercial on implementation handoff and identify expansion opportunities or renewal risks surfaced during delivery.

  • Represent the delivery perspective during pre-sales scoping of complex or higher-risk opportunities so commitments can be successfully delivered.

  • Drive structured post-onboarding Value Realization Projects, including complex migrations, integrations, optimization, remediation, and workflow initiatives.

  • Manage multiple concurrent implementations and make prioritization decisions based on risk, complexity, dependencies, and customer impact.

  • Identify opportunities to improve implementation processes, delivery predictability, time-to-value, and the overall customer experience.

What Makes You a Great Fit

Required

  • 3–5 years of experience in software implementation, customer onboarding, technical account or project management, or professional services, ideally within B2B SaaS, technology, or information services.

  • Demonstrated experience leading complex customer implementations with multiple workstreams, technical dependencies, contributors, or products.

  • Experience owning project scope, plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, change control, customer communication, and delivery outcomes.

  • Strong technical aptitude and the ability to understand configuration, data, integration, and technical delivery sufficiently to coordinate specialists and identify risk; coding is not required.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead customer conversations and communicate credibly with senior customer stakeholders.

  • Ability to lead and influence cross-functional contributors without formal authority.

  • Experience managing multiple concurrent projects and making informed prioritization decisions based on customer and business impact.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, analytical thinking, judgment, and problem-solving skills.

  • Proficiency with CRM tools such as Salesforce or HubSpot and Microsoft Office, with comfort using data, dashboards, and systems of record to communicate project health.

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and changing scope while maintaining accountability for outcomes.

  • Willingness to travel 10–20%.

Preferred

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, environmental science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • Experience with enterprise and/or mid-market SaaS customers.

  • Experience developing or improving implementation processes and customer journeys.

  • Familiarity with implementation, onboarding, or enablement tools such as Pendo, Gong, or Zendesk.

  • Experience working with time-to-value, adoption, usage, or customer health metrics.

  • Exposure to environmental, regulatory, compliance, chemical management, SDS, EHS, or sustainability software.

  • Multilingual capability and/or experience supporting global customers.

title: Staff Product Designer - Agentic Experiences
description: We design Spotify’s consumer experience end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints, from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify. Spotify's Core Experience (CoreX) team is shaping how listeners interact with Spotify through conversation, voice, and AI-powered experiences. We're building new ways for Premium subscribers to discover content, create playlists, control playback, and explore what they're listening to, using natural language. We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to help shape the future of these experiences. You'll lead the design direction for our conversational agent while staying close to the craft, designing and prototyping experiences that make AI feel useful, intuitive, and trustworthy. Working with product, engineering, machine learning, and design partners, you'll help create experiences that bring listeners closer to the audio and creators they love. What You'll Do Shape the experience strategy for Spotify's conversational agent, partnering with product, engineering, and data teams to create a shared design direction across multiple teams. Lead end-to-end product design for the core chat experience, from early exploration and prototyping through testing, refinement, and delivery. Define how conversational interactions work across Spotify, including when the agent responds, asks questions, offers choices, or helps listeners take action. Explore how conversation fits alongside familiar browsing and playback experiences across Home, Now Playing, and other key Spotify surfaces. Design intuitive voice and text interactions that support different listening contexts, including hands-free experiences, headphones, connected devices, and in-car listening. Create reusable interaction patterns and design guidance that help other teams bring conversational and AI-powered capabilities into their products. Partner with research, data science, and conversation design teams to evaluate experiences, understand listener behavior, and improve the product through evidence and experimentation. Build interactive prototypes to explore ideas, test assumptions, and make complex AI behaviors easier to understand and evaluate. Support and mentor designers across the program, share knowledge, and help teams make thoughtful design decisions that balance user needs, technical possibilities, and business goals. Who You Are You have experience leading product design for complex digital products, shaping design strategy, and bringing multiple teams together around a shared direction. You have worked on conversational, voice, or AI-powered experiences and understand how to design interactions that help people feel informed, confident, and in control. You bring strong interaction and visual design skills, with the ability to create consistent experiences across mobile, voice, and connected devices. You enjoy hands-on design and prototyping, using AI-enabled tools and emerging technologies to explore ideas, learn quickly, and communicate how an experience should work. You can turn complex or ambiguous challenges into clear design opportunities, using research, experimentation, and thoughtful judgment to guide decisions. You communicate ideas clearly, welcome different perspectives, and build collaborative relationships with designers, engineers, product partners, and senior stakeholders. You enjoy supporting other designers, sharing what you learn, and contributing to a team culture built on curiosity, creativity, and inclusion. Where You'll Be We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the Europe region as long as we have  a work location.  This team operates within the BST and CET time zone for collaboration. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.   At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>ABOUT QUINCE</strong></span></p> <p>Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes&nbsp; and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.</p> <p>What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>OUR CULTURE</strong></span></p> <p>Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.</p> <ul> <li>We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.&nbsp; Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.</li> <li>Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.&nbsp;</li> <li>Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.</p></div><p>Europe is Quince's next growth engine. We have launched in the UK, with further European markets on the roadmap, and organic discovery is one of the biggest untapped levers we have.</p> <p>We are looking for an SEO Manager, UK &amp; EU. You will own the organic strategy for our European markets across both traditional search and generative engines (AEO), building our European playbook.</p> <p>This is a cross-market, hands-on role with an unusual amount of ownership. Technical SEO standards and platform-level architecture come primarily from our global SEO team in the US; you are the person who translates those foundations into a European strategy, identifies where Europe needs something different, and makes the case for it. You will work day to day with storefront, copywriting, merchandising, growth marketing, engineering and data — and you will be the main driver for organic growth in the region.</p> <p>If you want to build an organic program from the ground up in markets where the brand is still being established, this is that job.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>What you'll do</strong></span></p> <ul> <li><strong>Own the UK/EU SEO &amp; AEO strategy.</strong> Build and maintain a market-level roadmap that reflects the real competitive dynamics of each country rather than a copy of the US plan. Decide where we play, which categories we go after first, and what winning looks like in each market.</li> <li><strong>Partner closely with the global SEO team.</strong> Adopt and apply global technical standards, feed European requirements into the global roadmap, and flag where a one-size-fits-all approach breaks down in-market.</li> <li><strong>Drive answer engine optimisation across Europe.</strong> Build Quince's presence in AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and the surfaces that follow. Own structured data coverage, entity and brand consistency, citation-worthy content, and the measurement approach that tells us whether any of it is working.</li> <li><strong>Make localisation a search advantage, not an afterthought.</strong> Work with copywriting and localisation to ensure category, PDP and editorial content targets genuine local search demand — not translated US keywords. Build the keyword and demand research foundation for each market and turn it into briefs writers can act on.</li> <li><strong>Own international search architecture in-market.</strong> Hreflang and market targeting, URL and domain structure, canonical logic, indexation of localised catalogues, and the crawl health of each European storefront — specced and QA'd with global SEO and engineering, with you accountable for the outcome.</li> <li><strong>Shape the storefront with merchandising and site merch.</strong> Influence category taxonomy, navigation, on-site search and PLP structure so that pages serve organic discovery as well as conversion. Partner on how content is modelled in our CMS and how listing pages are built and ranked.</li> <li><strong>Work in lockstep with growth marketing.</strong> Understand where organic and paid overlap, where they cannibalise, and where organic can take load off paid spend. Bring an incrementality mindset to the way we report and invest.</li> <li><strong>Own SEO/AEO readiness for new market launches.</strong> Define the checklist, run it, and make sure every new European storefront goes live search-ready rather than being retrofitted six months later.</li> <li><strong>Measure, report and build the case for investment.</strong> Own market-level organic reporting and the quarterly narrative for European and global leadership.</li> </ul> <h3>&nbsp;</h3> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Required experience</strong></span></p> <ul> <li>5+ years in SEO, ideally in ecommerce, retail or consumer brands, with meaningful ownership of organic performance.</li> <li>Demonstrable experience running SEO across more than one country or language.</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of technical SEO: crawl and indexation, site architecture, structured data, page performance.&nbsp;</li> <li>Content-led SEO experience: keyword and demand research, content strategy, briefing writers, and building category and editorial content that ranks and converts.</li> <li>Practical exposure to AEO — structured data, entity management, and a real point of view on how Quince should show up in AI-driven discovery.</li> <li>Comfortable in the data: Google Search Console, GA4, and the standard SEO toolset (Ahrefs, Semrush, Screaming Frog or similar).</li> <li>Excellent communicator in English, and effective working asynchronously with a headquarters team in another time zone.</li> <li>A bias for shipping. You are happy operating without a large team, deciding what matters most this quarter, and doing the work yourself.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Preferred</span></strong></p> <ul> <li>Working proficiency in English and, preferably, a second language (e.g. German, French, or Spanish).</li> <li>Experience launching ecommerce storefronts in new countries.</li> <li>Familiarity with headless CMS and search stacks (e.g. Contentful, Algolia) and translation management platforms (e.g. Smartling).</li> <li>Experience using AI-assisted tooling to produce or optimise content, metadata and structured data at scale.</li> <li>Apparel, home or lifestyle retail experience in the European market.</li> </ul> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Who you are</strong></span></p> <ul> <li>You think in systems. You would rather build a repeatable process that scales to five markets than win one category by hand.</li> <li>You are genuinely curious about how discovery is changing, and you are already testing how AI-driven search behaves in your own markets.</li> <li>You are persuasive without authority. Much of your impact comes from convincing merchandisers, writers, engineers and a global team to prioritise your work.</li> <li>You are commercially minded. You connect organic performance to revenue, not just to rankings.</li> <li>You are comfortable with ambiguity and with being early. title: Senior IT Analyst
description: About The Role The Senior IT Analyst is the principal in-house resource responsible for day-to-day IT support, providing first and second-line user support and day-to-day IT operations for approximately 80 users. As the principal person responsible for day-to-day IT operations, they will take ownership of incidents and service requests across the support lifecycle rather than operating solely as an escalation resource. This is a broad, senior analyst role for someone who is technically capable, comfortable working independently and able to manage competing priorities. The postholder will respond directly to users, resolve routine enquiries and requests, investigate more complex issues through to resolution and coordinate external technology suppliers where specialist expertise is needed. Alongside business-as-usual responsibilities, the role will support and deliver smaller technology projects and service improvements. By keeping FAIRR’s technology secure, reliable and easy to use, the role enables colleagues to focus on delivering FAIRR’s mission with investors and partners worldwide. Key Outcomes & Accountabilities OUTCOME 1: Users receive dependable, responsive IT support, with issues owned and resolved end to end Act as the principal in-house point of contact for day-to-day IT support, providing both first and second-line assistance according to operational needs. Resolve straightforward incidents and requests promptly, while taking the lead on more complex technical issues requiring deeper investigation and second-line expertise. Own and manage incidents and service requests from initial contact through to resolution, including access, software, equipment, permissions and non-standard user requirements, coordinating third-party suppliers or specialist support when required. Monitor recurring issues, identify root causes and implement practical improvements to reduce repeat incidents. Maintain accurate support records and produce clear information on service volumes, performance, trends and user experience. OUTCOME 2: Joiners, movers and leavers have the right access and equipment at the right time, and no more Coordinate all IT activities for joiners, movers and leavers in collaboration with HR and relevant managers. Create, amend and remove user accounts, licences, group memberships, permissions and application access accurately and on time, including removal of leaver access no later than the end of their last working day (or earlier where instructed by P&C). Prepare, issue, recover and securely manage laptops, mobile devices, peripherals and other IT equipment. Perform periodic access reviews and maintain appropriate evidence of approvals and completed actions. Manage shared, service and other non-person accounts, ensuring ownership, purpose and access are recorded. Where instructed by P&C or the Senior IT Manager, securely preserve or retrieve account and device data to support subject access requests, investigations or legal matters, maintaining confidentiality throughout. OUTCOME 3: IT changes are implemented in a controlled way with minimal disruption Plan, assess, document, communicate and implement routine IT changes in a controlled manner. Ensure changes have appropriate approvals, testing, implementation steps, back-out arrangements and post-change review where proportionate. Maintain the IT change schedule and coordinate activities to minimise disruption to users and business operations. Communicate planned changes clearly to affected users and stakeholders. Where changes need to take place outside normal working hours, schedule these in advance with the Senior IT Manager’s agreement (see Section 8). OUTCOME 4: IT services and workplace technology operate reliably and are used effectively and securely Administer Microsoft 365 and other cloud applications used by the organisation, including routine configuration, licence and user administration. Support laptops, mobile devices, meeting-room technology, printers, connectivity and standard workplace applications. Coordinate hardware repairs, replacements, warranty cases, software renewals and operational supplier activities. Maintain user guides, knowledge articles, standard operating procedures and support documentation. Provide practical guidance and training that helps users make effective and secure use of technology. OUTCOME 5: IT records, controls and evidence are complete, current and audit-ready Maintain complete and accurate asset, software, licence, supplier and other operational IT registers. Record equipment allocation, ownership, status, location, lifecycle and disposal information, and perform periodic reconciliations. Follow and help maintain IT policies, standards, procedures and control evidence. Complete routine operational checks and scheduled control activities, escalating risks, exceptions or control failures promptly. Support audits, reviews and compliance activities by providing accurate records and evidence. Handle devices, accounts and information in line with security, privacy and records-management requirements. Support compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025), including immediately escalating any suspected personal data breach to the Data Protection Lead so that the organisation can meet the 72-hour ICO reporting deadline where applicable. OUTCOME 6: Small projects and improvements are delivered and technology keeps getting better Deliver or support small IT projects, upgrades, application roll-outs and service improvements. Gather requirements, coordinate suppliers, plan user communications, support testing and manage implementation activities. Identify opportunities to improve reliability, security, efficiency and the user experience. Keep project actions, risks, decisions, documentation and handover materials up to date. Success Measures Success in the role will be assessed through: Service delivery Users receive dependable and responsive first and second-line technical support, with routine and complex issues resolved effectively. Incidents and requests are responded to and resolved within agreed service levels. User satisfaction with IT support is consistently positive. Accuracy, security and control Incidents, requests, access changes and joiner, mover and leaver activities are completed accurately and on time. 100% of leaver accounts disabled by the end of the last working day; new joiners fully equipped and set up on day one. Operational records, registers and control evidence are complete, current and reliable. Periodic access reviews and asset reconciliations completed on schedule with no significant audit findings. Change and improvement Changes and small projects are delivered in a controlled way with minimal disruption. Recurring problems are reduced and practical improvements are implemented continuously. Feedback from the Senior IT Manager, colleagues and suppliers on collaboration, communication and ownership. Technical Expertise & Role-Specific Capability Essential Strong hands-on experience providing both first and second-line IT support within a modern workplace environment, with particular strength in diagnosing and resolving more complex technical issues. Demonstrable experience managing a broad range of incidents and service requests through their full lifecycle, from initial user contact to resolution. Practical experience of joiner, mover and leaver processes, identity administration, permissions and access control. Experience administering Microsoft 365 and supporting Windows devices, laptops, mobile devices and common business applications. Experience maintaining IT asset records, operational registers, procedures and control evidence. Understanding of proportionate change management, information security and data protection practices. Ability to troubleshoot methodically, make sound decisions and know when to engage specialist support. Experience coordinating external IT suppliers and seeing actions through to completion. Ability to organise a varied workload independently and balance urgent support needs with planned operational work. Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical matters to non-technical users. Experience contributing to or delivering small IT projects and technology changes. Desirable Experience in a small organisation where the role covers a broad range of operational IT responsibilities. Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Autopilot, SharePoint and Teams administration. Experience with IT service management tools and ITIL-aligned working practices. Experience supporting SaaS applications and coordinating managed service, cyber security or other specialist partners. Relevant technical or service management certification (e.g. Microsoft 365 / Azure certifications, ITIL Foundation), or equivalent practical experience. Career Framework Expectations Our Career Framework provides a shared approach to development and performance across the organisation. It is built around four core pillars: Connect, Deliver, Focus and Lead, which outline the key behaviours and expectations expected at all levels. In this role, the pillars look like this: CONNECT — Building trust, relationships and collaboration Collaborative and able to build effective relationships with users, colleagues and suppliers. Technically credible, user-focused and committed to providing a high-quality service. DELIVER — Driving outcomes and execution Proactive and self-sufficient, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Calm and organised when handling competing priorities or service disruption. FOCUS — Applying expertise and driving improvement Detail-oriented and disciplined about keeping records, documentation and actions up to date. Curious and improvement-minded, with a willingness to learn and adapt. LEAD — Leading self, others and organisational success Practical and proportionate, applying appropriate control without unnecessary bureaucracy. Role-models secure and responsible use of technology and shares knowledge so colleagues become more self-sufficient. Organisational Values We are change makers: keeps the technology behind FAIRR’s work dependable, so colleagues can spend their time on the mission rather than on IT problems. We collaborate: works closely with HR, managers, colleagues and suppliers to deliver a joined-up service. We innovate: looks for better, simpler and more secure ways of working, and delivers improvements that last. We act with integrity: handles privileged access, devices and personal data responsibly, confidentially and transparently. Additional Information Working Arrangements Hybrid working from near Marble Arch (Oxford Street), London, UK, in line with FAIRR’s organisational working arrangements. Normal working hours are 9.00am–5.30pm, Monday to Friday. Because much of the role is hands-on (devices, meeting-room technology, joiner set-up), the postholder will be expected to work on site at least 3 days per week and on key operational days such as new starter inductions. Occasional work outside normal hours may be required for planned changes or urgent incidents. This will be agreed in advance wherever possible and recognised through time off in lieu in line with FAIRR policy. Travel Requirements Occasional travel within London and the UK may be required (e.g. supplier visits, training or events). International travel is not an expected part of the role. Salary Range To be confirmed during recruitment stage. Benefits Benefits will be provided in line with FAIRR’s standard employee benefits package. Pre-Employment Checks Appointment is subject to proof of the right to work in the UK, satisfactory references and, because the role holds privileged system access, a Basic DBS criminal record check. Information will be handled in line with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and data protection law. Equal Opportunities & Reasonable Adjustments FAIRR welcomes applications from all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process or in the role, please let us know. Performance & Flexibility This JD forms the basis for performance reviews. Performance against this JD will be reviewed during the 5-month probationary period and in regular one-to-ones thereafter. This job description is not exhaustive or contractual. The organisation reserves the right to modify duties and responsibilities to reflect organisational needs, subject to consultation where appropriate. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

  • Coordinate hardware repairs, replacements, warranty cases, software renewals and operational supplier activities.
  • Maintain user guides, knowledge articles, standard operating procedures and support documentation.
  • Provide practical guidance and training that helps users make effective and secure use of technology.
 
OUTCOME 5: IT records, controls and evidence are complete, current and audit-ready
  • Maintain complete and accurate asset, software, licence, supplier and other operational IT registers.
  • Record equipment allocation, ownership, status, location, lifecycle and disposal information, and perform periodic reconciliations.
  • Follow and help maintain IT policies, standards, procedures and control evidence.
  • Complete routine operational checks and scheduled control activities, escalating risks, exceptions or control failures promptly.
  • Support audits, reviews and compliance activities by providing accurate records and evidence.
  • Handle devices, accounts and information in line with security, privacy and records-management requirements.
  • Support compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025), including immediately escalating any suspected personal data breach to the Data Protection Lead so that the organisation can meet the 72-hour ICO reporting deadline where applicable.
 
OUTCOME 6: Small projects and improvements are delivered and technology keeps getting better
  • Deliver or support small IT projects, upgrades, application roll-outs and service improvements.
  • Gather requirements, coordinate suppliers, plan user communications, support testing and manage implementation activities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reliability, security, efficiency and the user experience.
  • Keep project actions, risks, decisions, documentation and handover materials up to date.


Success Measures

Success in the role will be assessed through:
 
Service delivery

  • Users receive dependable and responsive first and second-line technical support, with routine and complex issues resolved effectively.
  • Incidents and requests are responded to and resolved within agreed service levels.
  • User satisfaction with IT support is consistently positive.
Accuracy, security and control
  • Incidents, requests, access changes and joiner, mover and leaver activities are completed accurately and on time.
  • 100% of leaver accounts disabled by the end of the last working day; new joiners fully equipped and set up on day one.
  • Operational records, registers and control evidence are complete, current and reliable.
  • Periodic access reviews and asset reconciliations completed on schedule with no significant audit findings.
Change and improvement
  • Changes and small projects are delivered in a controlled way with minimal disruption.
  • Recurring problems are reduced and practical improvements are implemented continuously.
  • Feedback from the Senior IT Manager, colleagues and suppliers on collaboration, communication and ownership.


Technical Expertise & Role-Specific Capability

Essential

  • Strong hands-on experience providing both first and second-line IT support within a modern workplace environment, with particular strength in diagnosing and resolving more complex technical issues.
  • Demonstrable experience managing a broad range of incidents and service requests through their full lifecycle, from initial user contact to resolution.
  • Practical experience of joiner, mover and leaver processes, identity administration, permissions and access control.
  • Experience administering Microsoft 365 and supporting Windows devices, laptops, mobile devices and common business applications.
  • Experience maintaining IT asset records, operational registers, procedures and control evidence.
  • Understanding of proportionate change management, information security and data protection practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot methodically, make sound decisions and know when to engage specialist support.
  • Experience coordinating external IT suppliers and seeing actions through to completion.
  • Ability to organise a varied workload independently and balance urgent support needs with planned operational work.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical matters to non-technical users.
  • Experience contributing to or delivering small IT projects and technology changes.
 
Desirable
  • Experience in a small organisation where the role covers a broad range of operational IT responsibilities.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Autopilot, SharePoint and Teams administration.
  • Experience with IT service management tools and ITIL-aligned working practices.
  • Experience supporting SaaS applications and coordinating managed service, cyber security or other specialist partners.
  • Relevant technical or service management certification (e.g. Microsoft 365 / Azure certifications, ITIL Foundation), or equivalent practical experience.


Career Framework Expectations

Our Career Framework provides a shared approach to development and performance across the organisation. It is built around four core pillars: Connect, Deliver, Focus and Lead, which outline the key behaviours and expectations expected at all levels.
In this role, the pillars look like this:

CONNECT — Building trust, relationships and collaboration

  • Collaborative and able to build effective relationships with users, colleagues and suppliers.
  • Technically credible, user-focused and committed to providing a high-quality service.
DELIVER — Driving outcomes and execution
  • Proactive and self-sufficient, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
  • Calm and organised when handling competing priorities or service disruption.
FOCUS — Applying expertise and driving improvement
  • Detail-oriented and disciplined about keeping records, documentation and actions up to date.
  • Curious and improvement-minded, with a willingness to learn and adapt.
LEAD — Leading self, others and organisational success
  • Practical and proportionate, applying appropriate control without unnecessary bureaucracy.
  • Role-models secure and responsible use of technology and shares knowledge so colleagues become more self-sufficient.


Organisational Values

  1. We are change makers: keeps the technology behind FAIRR’s work dependable, so colleagues can spend their time on the mission rather than on IT problems.
  2. We collaborate: works closely with HR, managers, colleagues and suppliers to deliver a joined-up service.
  3. We innovate: looks for better, simpler and more secure ways of working, and delivers improvements that last.
  4. We act with integrity: handles privileged access, devices and personal data responsibly, confidentially and transparently.


Additional Information

Working Arrangements
Hybrid working from near Marble Arch (Oxford Street), London, UK, in line with FAIRR’s organisational working arrangements.
 
Normal working hours are 9.00am–5.30pm, Monday to Friday. Because much of the role is hands-on (devices, meeting-room technology, joiner set-up), the postholder will be expected to work on site at least 3 days per week and on key operational days such as new starter inductions.
 
Occasional work outside normal hours may be required for planned changes or urgent incidents. This will be agreed in advance wherever possible and recognised through time off in lieu in line with FAIRR policy.

Travel Requirements
Occasional travel within London and the UK may be required (e.g. supplier visits, training or events). International travel is not an expected part of the role.

Salary Range
To be confirmed during recruitment stage.

Benefits
Benefits will be provided in line with FAIRR’s standard employee benefits package.

Pre-Employment Checks
Appointment is subject to proof of the right to work in the UK, satisfactory references and, because the role holds privileged system access, a Basic DBS criminal record check. Information will be handled in line with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and data protection law.
 
Equal Opportunities & Reasonable Adjustments
FAIRR welcomes applications from all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process or in the role, please let us know.

Performance & Flexibility

  • This JD forms the basis for performance reviews.
  • Performance against this JD will be reviewed during the 5-month probationary period and in regular one-to-ones thereafter.
  • This job description is not exhaustive or contractual. The organisation reserves the right to modify duties and responsibilities to reflect organisational needs, subject to consultation where appropriate.

What you bring You’ll thrive in this role if you have: Significant experience designing and improving financial crime frameworks, controls and operating models in the UK or EU Experience across multiple entities and jurisdictions, covering UK and EU/EEA requirements Experience managing specialists while staying hands-on A track record of leading change end to end, from stakeholders to delivery Demonstrable experience driving innovation, for example AI-enabled workflows or automated controls The ability to turn complex financial crime concepts into clear, practical guidance It’s a bonus if you have: Led a screening vendor migration or a similar system implementation Hands-on experience preparing for the EU AML Regulation You might come from a fintech or a bank. raw.title: Product Manager - Integrations
raw.description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

As a Product Manager - Integration, you’ll bring hands-on accounting expertise into a product environment to shape integrations that match real finance workflows. You’ll sit in our Accounting Integrations team and help ensure spend data (expenses, receipts, VAT, categories) flows cleanly from Pleo into the accounting systems and ERPs finance teams rely on, with minimal manual work. This is a hybrid role at the intersection of accounting domain knowledge, product thinking and technical partner collaboration, where your judgement will directly influence what we build and how it lands for customers.

You’ll own a portfolio of integrations and partners, turning customer needs and operational edge cases into clear requirements and improvements delivered with internal teams and external developers. Success in this role shows up in higher export success rates, fewer configuration-related issues and integrations that finance teams can trust at month-end.

Who you'll be working with and reporting to

You’ll be part of the Accounting Integrations team, focused on connecting Pleo with the accounting systems and ERPs most used by European finance teams.
You will report to our Group Product Manager from Integrations and will work closely with Product and Engineering to define requirements, make sound accounting decisions and support delivery across many different systems and data models.
You’ll also collaborate with external development partners and ERP vendors building on Pleo’s APIs, acting as a key point of contact to keep implementations on track and aligned with customer workflows.

What you'll be doing

As an Product Manager you will:

  • Own a portfolio of accounting integrations and partner relationships, balancing customer needs, partner requests and internal priorities.

  • Translate export, reconciliation and month-end close workflows into clear product requirements and integration behaviours.

  • Partner with engineers to define data mapping and implementation details across multiple accounting systems, data models and APIs.

  • Improve the integration set-up and configuration experience so customers can onboard successfully with fewer issues.

  • Act as a trusted accounting domain expert, making pragmatic decisions that improve data quality and reduce manual work for finance teams.

  • Support external partners and ERP vendors building on Pleo’s APIs, ensuring alignment on expectations, delivery and quality.

  • Track and improve outcomes such as export success rate, adoption/activation and integration-related support volume.

What you bring

Must have

  • Practical bookkeeping and finance process knowledge (expense coding, reconciliation and month-end close).

  • Strong understanding of how accountants, bookkeepers and finance leads work day to day.

  • A solid track record working with product teams from defining requirements through to delivery.

  • Experience managing external partners or senior stakeholders and delivering through influence.

  • Hands-on exposure to technology in a finance context (for example configuring accounting/ERP tools, working with integrations/data imports, or collaborating closely with technical teams).

Nice to have

  • Experience with European accounting and ERP systems, and/or an accounting qualification.

  • Partner negotiation experience and/or additional European languages.

  • Working knowledge of APIs, data mapping or implementation projects.

Why this role is a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You enjoy bringing real accounting expertise into product decisions and can explain complex finance concepts in a clear, practical way.

  • You like owning problems end to end - from identifying the right solution to working with others to ship it.

  • You’re motivated by improving workflows for finance teams and can connect day-to-day pain points to measurable outcomes.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You want a role where you control delivery directly, rather than delivering through internal teams and external partners.

  • You prefer depth in a single system over context switching across many tools, markets and accounting practices.

  • You’re looking for a purely accounting or purely technical role, without the “bridge” work in between.

How you'll develop in this role

Within your first 6 months, you’ll build a deep understanding of customer export and reconciliation needs and how Pleo’s integrations behave in practice, then take ownership of a defined portfolio of integrations and partners. You’ll identify the highest-impact improvements to the integration set-up experience and drive them to delivery with internal teams.


Within 12 months, you’ll be a go-to expert for integration and accounting decisions, with measurable improvements in export success rates and a reduction in configuration-related issues. You’ll help launch new or improved integrations by enabling internal teams and partners with the context and clarity they need to deliver well.

Over time, you’ll strengthen your product toolkit (requirements, trade-offs, delivery rituals) and build deeper technical fluency by working side-by-side with engineers on real integration complexity.


Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Please note: Applications for this role will close on Wednesday, October 13th to ensure our team has enough time to give every candidate's application the care and attention it deserves.

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  • Intro Call (30 min): A conversation with a Talent Acquisition Partner to provide a high-level overview of Pleo and the role, confirm essential skills, and gauge initial alignment.

  • Hiring Manager Interview (45 min): A discussion with your future manager to evaluate your functional expertise, past experience, and role fit.

  • Pleo Challenge (60 min): A role-specific "live session" based on a scenario or business dilemma completed with key stakeholders.

Transparency is important to us

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we're looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

  • CV writing and content: AI can be useful for structure, but generic AI-written CVs often hide your real impact. We’re more likely to engage when you share specific outcomes (for example: “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z”) and explain the context around your decisions.

  • Application care: Our talent team reads every application. Taking a few minutes to tailor your answers and highlight the most relevant examples will genuinely help you stand out.

  • Profile to role fit: This role is best suited to someone who can combine practical accounting knowledge with product thinking and proactive ownership. We’ll be looking for evidence that you understand finance workflows like reconciliation and month-end close, can translate those needs into clear requirements, and are comfortable collaborating with technical teams and external partners to deliver high-quality integrations.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

raw.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - MX
raw.description:
Forward Deployed Engineer - Mexico

About the Company

We're partnering with an AI-native operating system for supply chains used by wholesalers, manufacturers, retailers, and traders. The platform integrates logistics and procurement data through connections with internal and external systems, enabling predictive analytics and automated workflows that improve fill rates, reduce inventory levels, and optimize cash-to-cash cycle time.

By leveraging predictive analytics and automation, the company helps large enterprises reduce costs, unlock additional revenue, and prevent under- or over-stocking across complex global supply chains.

Role Overview

The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is the person who makes the platform work in the real world. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, client operations, and AI implementation — and owns the technical execution of how the platform gets built into each client's environment.

The FDE works directly with clients and the Implementation team, learns how each client's systems and operations actually run, and builds the integrations, automations, and AI solutions that make the platform mission-critical. This is a first-of-its-kind role at the company — the person who takes it will be defining what forward deployment looks like here.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build integrations between the platform and client systems — ERPs, WMS, TMS, data warehouses — writing real code to connect, extract, and transform data across environments

  • Deploy alongside clients in their environment — understand how their teams actually operate, where data breaks, and what needs to be built or configured to run reliably

  • Design, implement, and iterate on AI workflows using the company's platform — agentic flows, prompt engineering, context design, and output evaluation — tuned to each client's specific supply chain use cases

  • Own the reliability, performance, and continuous improvement of live deployments — monitor outputs, identify failure modes, and fix them without waiting to be asked

  • Translate what you build and learn in the field into structured product feedback, technical documentation, and reusable playbooks — so the next deployment starts smarter than the last

Profile We're Looking For

  • You build things: Min. 2-4 years of hands-on engineering experience — Python, REST APIs, SQL — and a portfolio of real integrations or systems you've shipped, not just designed

  • You operate in ambiguity: comfortable walking into a client environment without a complete spec, asking the right questions, and figuring out what needs to be built — without waiting for perfect requirements

  • You understand data end-to-end: how it flows across systems, where it breaks, and what it takes to make it clean and reliable enough for AI to use — SQL or equivalent is second nature

  • You have a working understanding of AI and LLMs: enough to design prompts, evaluate outputs critically, and know when a model result looks right but isn't

  • You communicate clearly across audiences: can explain a technical integration to a VP of Operations and write clean documentation for an engineer — in both Spanish and English

  • You own what you ship: high accountability, low ego — you track down the root cause, fix it, and make sure it doesn't happen again

  • Based in LATAM or the US, available to work across time zones and travel to client sites when needed

Nice to Have

  • Background in supply chain, logistics, or operations — you'll understand what stockouts, fill rates, and OTIF mean without needing a glossary

  • Experience integrating with enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, or similar ERPs and WMS platforms

  • Previous experience in a forward-deployed, solutions engineering, or customer-facing technical role

Tu travailles de manière autonome tout en gardant le cap fixé, sais t'approprier des objectifs précis et mets tout en œuvre pour les atteindre. Tu sais concevoir des actions spécifiques , adaptées à la fois aux besoins de tes partenaires et à la stratégie définie par ton manager. Nous progressons rapidement, nous explorons toujours de nouvelles idées et nous sommes très transparents quant aux décisions que nous prenons et à ce qui motive nos choix. Il y a tellement de questions que nous souhaitons résoudre, et encore plus que nous n'avons pas encore rencontrées. Comment les données et la technologie peuvent-elles aider les restaurants à développer leur activité à mesure que les habitudes des consommateurs évoluent ? Comment pouvons-nous prédire ce qu'une personne souhaitera pour dîner avant même que l'idée ne lui vienne à l'esprit ? Chez Deliveroo, ces questions ne sont que quelques-uns des défis ambitieux auxquels nous nous efforçons de répondre – et il n'y a aucun projet qui ne peut pas devenir le vôtre. Aucune solution n'appartient à une équipe en particulier, ce qui vous ouvre d'extraordinaires possibilités en termes de développement et d'impact personnel. Avec un score de 99/100 à l'Indice de l'Égalité Hommes-Femmes 2023, nous sommes engagés envers l'égalité des chances. Rejoignez-nous avec votre passion pour la nourriture dans une entreprise en pleine croissance. Deep, hands-on familiarity with the current AI coding tooling landscape: agentic coding tools, LLM-powered code review, prompt engineering for development workflows, MCP ecosystems, and what's coming next. You're a natural communicator who can discuss a trade-off with a skeptical senior engineer just as well as you can help a junior developer get started. Comfortable working in a remote-first, async culture with teams across multiple time zones; clear communicator in English. Autonomy and ownership mindset: you drive this agenda without waiting for direction, and you bring others with you rather than working alone. Bonus: experience with open-source communities, cybersecurity domain knowledge, contributions to AI tooling projects, or public writing/speaking on AI-Native engineering. 🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job. We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company , and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation . You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem. ⭐ Be part of something bigger We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative. 💻 Work at the edge of what’s next We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice. 🌍 Global opportunity without borders Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. Lemonway est un établissement de paiement agréé, au cœur de la nouvelle économie européenne.

Nous sécurisons les paiements des plateformes de financement participatif, d’économie collaborative, des marketplaces et des e-commerçants, avec un fort engagement contre la fraude et pour la protection des fonds.

Réglementée par l’ACPR et bénéficiant du passeport européen dans 29 pays, Lemonway est basée à Paris et Hambourg et rassemble 150 Lemonheroes multiculturels et engagés.

Plus de 400 marketplaces nous font confiance. Nous gérons 1,4 million de portefeuilles utilisateurs et avons levé 50 M€ auprès de Breega, SpeedInvest et Toscafund.

Rentable depuis quatre ans et en croissance de +25 % en 2025, Lemonway vise à rester parmi les leaders du paiement en Europe grâce à une croissance saine et durable.

  • Tu as idéalement travaillé sur des projets en lien avec des systèmes comme Apache Kafka, Rabbitmq...

title: Alternant·e Growth Marketing Manager | Thiga Academy
description: Alternance · Paris 9e · Télétravail · rythme d’alternance souhaité 3 semaines entreprise / 1 semaine école    Thiga en 30 secondes :  Thiga est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en IA et en digital. Nous accompagnons les plus grands groupes et scale-ups françaises : Decathlon, Doctolib, AXA, ManoMano, Mirakl, Disney, Leboncoin et une centaine d'autres. Nous sommes 200, majoritairement à Paris. Thiga Academy, c'est notre organisme de formation. On y forme les équipes produit (Product Managers, Product Owners, Designers, Product Leaders) et celles qui veulent le devenir : product management, product discovery, leadership produit, et IA appliquée au produit. En inter-entreprise comme en intra, on transmet ce que nos consultants pratiquent chez nos clients tous les jours   Pourquoi ce poste :  L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite. C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir. Ce que tu vas faire 🖇 1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing & Events Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence 2. Mesurer, analyser, arbitrer Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires. Suivre les KPIs qui comptent à chaque étape du tunnel : trafic, taux de clic, taux de conversion en lead, taux de conversion en inscrit, coût d'acquisition par inscrit, taux de remplissage des sessions Construire les dashboards HubSpot qui donnent une vision claire de ce qui marche, canal par canal, campagne par campagne Identifier où le tunnel fuit et proposer les hypothèses à tester pour colmater Faire remonter les résultats au Head of Marketing & Events pour arbitrer les prochains messages, offres et canaux, avec des chiffres, pas des impressions 3. Faire vivre la marque et la communauté qui nourrissent le funnel L'acquisition ne marche pas sans contenu ni preuve sociale. C'est le carburant du tunnel. Poser la ligne éditoriale et la faire vivre : posts LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, formats courts autour du product et de l'IA Animer la relation avec les alumni et la communauté d'apprenants : témoignages, cas concrets, un bouche-à-oreille qu'on peut transformer en canal d'acquisition mesurable L'IA n'est pas une option chez nous , c'est la pierre angulaire de notre façon de travailler, et on attend de toi que tu aies cette fibre. Concrètement, tu t'appuieras sur l'IA à chaque étape : générer et itérer des variantes de copies avec Claude, produire des visuels avec Nano Banana et Figma, des teasers avec HeyGen, ou transformer une transcription Granola en article et en carrousel LinkedIn. C'est ce qui te permet d'avancer vite et de tester dix fois plus d'hypothèses qu'une équipe classique. La stack que tu vas pratiquer 🧰 Le growth marketing moderne, c'est une combinaison d'intuition testée par la donnée, de vitesse d'exécution et de bons outils au bon moment. LLM et agents : Claude (Pro et Code), Gemini Génération visuelle et audio : Nano Banana, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, HeyGen Marketing ops : HubSpot (CRM, marketing hub, workflows), Luma, Phantom Buster Prise de notes et capitalisation : Granola, Notion AI Vibe coding (en bonus, pour les profils qui veulent aller plus loin) : Lovable, Cursor pour bricoler des micro-outils internes Tu n'as pas besoin de tout maîtriser à l'arrivée. On attend une vraie curiosité et l'envie de pratiquer, pas un CV exhaustif. Le profil que nous recherchons 🌟 Formation : école de commerce ou de communication, en M1 ou M2, idéalement avec une spécialisation marketing, growth ou entrepreneuriat Pratique IA personnelle prouvée : tu as un side project, un compte ChatGPT ou Claude que tu utilises tous les jours, un workflow Make ou n8n que tu as construit, un agent custom, un blog assisté par LLM, un repo GitHub, ou n'importe quoi qui démontre que l'IA est dans ta vie. Réflexe growth : tu penses en funnel avant de penser en campagne, tu formules des hypothèses avant de produire, et tester puis mesurer te vient plus naturellement que produire pour produire Appétence data : Excel ou Google Sheets n'ont pas de secret pour toi, et l'idée de creuser un dashboard pour comprendre pourquoi un taux de conversion a bougé t'intéresse plus qu'elle ne t'ennuie Fibre communication : tu sais écrire pour être lu, tu as déjà animé une page, un compte ou une communauté Rigueur opérationnelle et sens du détail : tu sais qu'une séquence email qui commence par « Bonjour {prénom} », ça fait tâche, et qu'un A/B test mal cadré ne prouve rien Sensibilité business : tu comprends les concepts MQL, CAC, NPS, et tu sais qu'une belle campagne ne vaut rien si elle ne remplit pas les sessions Au-delà des hard skills, on recherche surtout quelqu’un de curieux, volontaire, débrouillard et qui n’a pas peur de proposer des nouvelles idées ! Ce qu'on offre 🎊 Stack IA premium : Claude, Gemini, et accès facilité à tous les outils IA quand ils sont pertinents pour ton travail Encadrement et présence au quotidien de membres de l'équipe marketing pointus sur les sujets growth, événementiel et IA Cadence de suivi : 1-to-1 hebdomadaire avec le Head of Marketing & Events. Fonctionnement quotidien en équipe avec les autres Head of (Content, Design) et le CMO Cadre de travail : bureaux 23 rue Taitbout (Paris 9), équipe marketing de 8 personnes Rémunération : grille légale alternance, transparente dès l'entretien Le process 🎢 Envoie ton CV, un lien vers un side project ou portfolio (même bricolé). Pas de lettre de motivation. En termes de déroulé, tu auras :  Un premier call avec notre Talent Acquisition Manager Un échange avec le Head of Marketing & Event  Un case study à préparer et présenter  Un dernier entretien avec Hugo, notre CEO Thiga accueille toutes les personnes compétentes et passionnées et s'engage en faveur de la diversité culturelle, l'égalité de genre et l'emploi des travailleurs handicapés — au contraire nous considérons la diversité comme une grande richesse ! raw.title: Insurance Risk & Strategy
raw.description:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⭐️ The Insurance Team ⭐️

Being part of Alan's insurance community is a great opportunity to have a significant impact on people's health and wellbeing in our multiple countries of operation.

  • We are at the heart of Alan’s mission, bringing to the team our technical leadership and expertise on healthcare and death & disability insurance.

  • We work hand in hand with our data scientists, designers, engineers and product managers to build the most differentiating products and provide a delightful experience at a fair price.

  • We build and manage offers for large companies and public institutions with our sales and account management teams.

  • We make sure our portfolio is closely monitored and risks are effectively managed.

  • We also manage our capital, steer our reinsurance strategy and maintain a trusting relationship with our insurance regulators.

⭐️ Your role ⭐️ ️

As Alan’s Risk Expert, you will be in charge of providing Alan with automated and scalable risk assessment tools:

  • Risk modeling

    • You will be in charge of strengthening and automating the building our Solvency 2 balance sheet and capital requirements projections, covering both health, death and disability business lines

    • You will model new risks when they arise (new insurance products, branches, international, investment etc.)

    • You will challenge our risk appetite, propose new relevant risk metrics and build tools to monitor them

    • You will support the board meetings preparation and communication with investors regarding capital evolution and market risks

  • Regulatory

    • You will scale and automate the production of our regulatory quantitative reporting and contribute to our narrative (SFCR, RSR) and ORSA reports

    • You will support our discussions with supervisors

    • You will assist the assessment of international opportunities and help prepare the opening of new countries

  • Capital management

    • You will make proposals to improve our capital management in the 4 countries Alan is present

    • You will manage our reinsurance strategy, to find an optimum between solvency and profitability, negotiating with reinsurance partners, and analyze reinsurance reporting

  • Team Growth

    • You will create processes and resources to strengthen the team’s ability to understand our risk and capital constraints

    • You will support the identification and hiring of new talents for the Insurance and Risk teams.

⭐️ Is it you we’re looking for? ⭐️

You would thrive in this role if you:

  • Have at last 8 years of experience in Solvency 2 regulatory framework, especially for S2 accounting, with knowledge of Health, Life and Market risks as a bonus

  • Are fluent in English and in French for regulatory interactions

  • Possess excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, including data analysis capabilities

  • Can automate processes and build new tools, with programming skills being a plus

  • Bring rigor and reliability to reporting production while working independently in a fast-paced environment

  • Have strong communication skills for effective interaction with internal and external stakeholders

  • Are confident learning new tools, technologies, and methodologies with creative problem-solving approaches

For this position, we are looking to hire someone within the D-F level.

🙌 Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer:

  • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary.

  • Flexible Office. Amazing office space at our HQ, sponsored co-working hubs or a full-remote experience with home office equipment sponsorship, we want you to live where you’re the happiest.

  • All the tools you need. Top of the range equipment: Macbook Pro, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. organize your time as you wish.

Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

Il y a vingt ans, les premières sélections Les Composantes voyaient le jour. Une histoire née d’une soif d’indépendance et d’une passion pour le vintage. Une manière instinctive de faire circuler les vêtements, guidée par une attention particulière à ce qui dure.

Dans son prolongement, Sézane prend vie en 2013 : la première marque de mode française née en ligne. Puis sont venus enrichir cet univers : Octobre Éditions pour les hommes, Les Composantes, dédiée cette fois à l’art de vivre, et Petit Sézane pour les enfants.

Tout s’est construit comme on avance dans la vie : par élans, par gestes spontanés avec cette manière d’apprendre en faisant. Une autre relation au détail, au service et au lien. Une autre manière d’habiller le réel, d’abord en ligne, puis à travers nos Appartements.

Nous recherchons aujourd’hui des talents créatifs, structurés et agiles qui partagent l’envie d’améliorer sans cesse tout ce qui peut l’être. Des talents passionnés, autonomes qui conçoivent le travail dans le respect des autres et pour qui rien n'est hors d'atteinte, pour peu qu'on s'en donne les moyens.

Envie d’imaginer la suite de cette histoire à nos côtés ? Ecrivez-nous !


Nous recherchons les talents d’un(e) Retail Merchandiser Europe en CDD à partir de maintenant, pour une durée de 6 mois minimum (H/F) pour rejoindre nos équipes. Ce poste est basé à Paris (75).

Intégré(e) au sein du pôle Retail, rattaché(e) à la Head of Retail Merchandising vos principales missions seront les suivantes :

  • Collaborer à la création de l’assortiment par boutique en entrée de saison (collection permanente et saisonnière) puis à son actualisation hebdomadaire pour chaque lancement de collection, en lien avec le calendrier commercial web (adaptation au lieu, à la clientèle, à la saisonnalité, aux remontées des équipes locales, etc.) ;
  • Définir les niveaux d’implantation cible des nouveautés par catégorie et boutique ;
  • Réaliser des analyses ad-hoc sur la performance de l’offre pour mettre en place des plans d’action concrets à court ou moyen terme ;
  • Interagir avec les points de vente de manière hebdomadaire pour les demandes d’ajustement de l’assortiment (demandes d’ajout, de retour…) ;
  • Coordonner les propositions de produit, envois d'échantillons, validation des légendes pour nos partenaires Grands Magasins et Presse ;
  • Construire les listes et coordonner, en lien étroit avec l’équipe approvisionnement retail, les retours inter-saison et fin de saison. Gérer les ajustements des besoins de stocks ;
  • Participer aux visites de points de vente (floor et stock) afin de mettre en place des plans d’action visant à optimiser la satisfaction client ;
  • Apporter un support à l’ouverture des nouvelles adresses permanentes et pop-ups.

Requirements

  • Diplômé(e) d'une école de mode ou d’une école de commerce avec spécialisation mode, ou de son équivalent universitaire ;
  • Vous mettez en avant une expérience de minimum 5 ans sur un poste équivalent au sein d'une marque de prêt-à-porter ;
  • Vous disposez d’une forte sensibilité produit combinée à un œil business pragmatique ;
  • Vous êtes curieux(euse), proactif(ive) avec un sens entrepreneurial ;
  • Vous maitrisez Excel et avez un goût prononcé pour l’analyse de données ;
  • Vous êtes très organisé(e) et la gestion des priorités n'a pas de secret pour vous !
  • Anglais courant indispensable.


Vous vous êtes reconnu(e) dans ce descriptif et souhaitez rejoindre l’aventure Sézane ? Alors n’attendez plus !
