title: Head of Hardware
description: Accelerating embodied AGI. The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century. MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data. We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries. Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Head of Hardware, you own that hardware end to end: electrical, firmware, and the mechanical integration that holds it together, from the first schematic to devices running on factory floors. You lead the team that builds it. Today that is about six engineers on robotics, three on EMG sensing, and three on camera systems, plus contractors, and it will grow quickly. Our Electrical Engineer and Embedded Engineer roles report to you. You set the architecture they build against, and you still build alongside them. This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage. What You Will Do Own the hardware roadmap for Shift and Atlas data capture: wearables, sensor rigs, camera systems, and prototype robots. What we build, in what order, and why. Set the system architecture across electrical, firmware, and mechanical: sensors, compute, power, wireless, and enclosures. Make the trade-offs, and make them stick when disciplines disagree. Stay on the bench: schematics, layout reviews, board bring-up, and a scope in your hands when the team is stuck. On the days it matters, you are the best electrical engineer in the room. Lead and grow the team: hire, set the bar, run design reviews, and give engineers ownership of whole subsystems rather than tickets. Guarantee data quality end to end: EMG and EEG front ends, camera pipelines, IMUs, and synchronization across many devices, so that what reaches the ML team is clean, time-aligned, and trustworthy. Take designs from prototype to small-batch production: DFM, component and EMS vendors, test fixtures, certification, and field reliability. Work shoulder to shoulder with ML and deployment. Your hardware decides what the training data looks like, and you will be on the floor where it is captured. Run contractors and partners without losing ownership of the result. Requirements You have taken at least one product from zero to shipped, with significant ownership of the outcome: as a co-founder, CTO, first hardware hire, or the lead who owned the whole device. Not one subsystem, not one phase. Ideally a wearable, at a tier-one hardware company known for shipping at scale. Electrical engineering is your home discipline. You have designed boards that shipped, across mixed-signal, power, wireless, and high-speed digital, and you can still do it today. You think in systems. You understand how an electrode choice, an enclosure tolerance, and an ADC sample rate interact, and you can hold the mechanical and firmware conversations as a peer, not a customer. You have led engineers: hired them, grown them, and kept a team shipping through 0-to-1 ambiguity. Typically 6+ years in hardware, but we care more about what you shipped than how long it took. A strong understanding of how hardware decisions affect data quality. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you design accordingly. Experience taking hardware to small-batch production: DFM, vendor and EMS management, test, and certification. Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice. High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. A 0-to-1 hardware program takes the hours it takes, in person and at pace, and you have chosen that before. Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care. Nice to Have Wearables, smartwatches, drones, robotics, AR/VR, or defense wearables on your résumé. Camera systems: sensor selection, MIPI and ISP pipelines, and multi-camera synchronization. Low-power and battery design, BLE or Wi-Fi, and antenna integration in small enclosures. Enough mechanical fluency (CAD, tolerances, and materials) to challenge the mechanical team’s choices and be right some of the time. Prior founder or founding-engineer experience, including the parts that went wrong. Open-source hardware or firmware contributions. Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits: Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it. Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it. Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them. Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes. This is for you if: You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec. You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one. You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do. This is not for you if: You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5. You would forward output you cannot explain. "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer. How We Hire We read every application and reply within five working days. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem. Then a decision, usually within a few days. Pay Transparency Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting. What We Offer Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter. Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval. A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage. Free food and drinks in the office. Equal Opportunity MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity. This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage.

What You Will Do

  • Own the hardware roadmap for Shift and Atlas data capture: wearables, sensor rigs, camera systems, and prototype robots. What we build, in what order, and why.

  • Set the system architecture across electrical, firmware, and mechanical: sensors, compute, power, wireless, and enclosures. Make the trade-offs, and make them stick when disciplines disagree.

  • Stay on the bench: schematics, layout reviews, board bring-up, and a scope in your hands when the team is stuck. On the days it matters, you are the best electrical engineer in the room.

  • Lead and grow the team: hire, set the bar, run design reviews, and give engineers ownership of whole subsystems rather than tickets.

  • Guarantee data quality end to end: EMG and EEG front ends, camera pipelines, IMUs, and synchronization across many devices, so that what reaches the ML team is clean, time-aligned, and trustworthy.

  • Take designs from prototype to small-batch production: DFM, component and EMS vendors, test fixtures, certification, and field reliability.

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with ML and deployment. Your hardware decides what the training data looks like, and you will be on the floor where it is captured.

  • Run contractors and partners without losing ownership of the result.

Requirements

  • You have taken at least one product from zero to shipped, with significant ownership of the outcome: as a co-founder, CTO, first hardware hire, or the lead who owned the whole device. Not one subsystem, not one phase. Ideally a wearable, at a tier-one hardware company known for shipping at scale.

  • Electrical engineering is your home discipline. You have designed boards that shipped, across mixed-signal, power, wireless, and high-speed digital, and you can still do it today.

  • You think in systems. You understand how an electrode choice, an enclosure tolerance, and an ADC sample rate interact, and you can hold the mechanical and firmware conversations as a peer, not a customer.

  • You have led engineers: hired them, grown them, and kept a team shipping through 0-to-1 ambiguity. Typically 6+ years in hardware, but we care more about what you shipped than how long it took.

  • A strong understanding of how hardware decisions affect data quality. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you design accordingly.

  • Experience taking hardware to small-batch production: DFM, vendor and EMS management, test, and certification.

  • Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice.

  • High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. A 0-to-1 hardware program takes the hours it takes, in person and at pace, and you have chosen that before.

  • Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care.

Nice to Have

  • Wearables, smartwatches, drones, robotics, AR/VR, or defense wearables on your résumé.

  • Camera systems: sensor selection, MIPI and ISP pipelines, and multi-camera synchronization.

  • Low-power and battery design, BLE or Wi-Fi, and antenna integration in small enclosures.

  • Enough mechanical fluency (CAD, tolerances, and materials) to challenge the mechanical team’s choices and be right some of the time.

  • Prior founder or founding-engineer experience, including the parts that went wrong.

  • Open-source hardware or firmware contributions.

Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

  • Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

  • Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

  • Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

  • Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if:

  • You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

  • You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

  • You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if:

  • You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

  • You would forward output you cannot explain.

  • "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

  1. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

  2. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

  3. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

  4. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

  5. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

  • Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

  • Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

  • A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

  • Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.

Wir verstehen Strategie und Design nicht als getrennte Disziplinen, sondern als gegenseitige Enabler, die für Unternehmen und Marken nachhaltig Wert schaffen. Gesucht werden Persönlichkeiten, die sich gerne in ein dynamisches Umfeld einbringen und Freude daran haben, gemeinsam mit anderen Talenten Lösungen zu entwickeln, die die Erwartungen an eine klassische Agentur übertreffen. On-site, 1–2 Tage Homeoffice möglich


Deine Aufgaben

  • Ausarbeitung und Weiterentwicklung von visuellen Identitäten, Corporate Designs und Designsystemen
  • Gestaltung und Weiterentwicklung von Logos, Logo-Systemen, Brand Guidelines, Typografie- und Farbsystemen sowie Bildwelten
  • Entwicklung digitaler Markenanwendungen, insbesondere Websites, Responsive Designs und digitale Designsysteme
  • Gestaltung von Kommunikationsmitteln und Markenanwendungen über Touchpoints wie Web, Social Media, Kampagne, Motion und Print
  • Präzise Umsetzung von Designkonzepten und Sicherstellung einer konsistenten visuellen Markenführung
  • Zusammenarbeit mit Art Directors, Strateg:innen und Berater:innen bei der Entwicklung starker und umsetzbarer Lösungen
  • Einbringen eigener Ideen und aktives Mitdenken bei kreativen und gestalterischen Fragestellungen
  • Aufbereitung und Präsentation von Entwürfen und Varianten im Team sowie gegebenenfalls gegenüber Kund:innen
  • Aktive Nutzung und Weiterentwicklung deiner Kenntnisse in Figma, Adobe Creative Suite und neuen Design-Tools
  • Bereitschaft, dich in strategische und unternehmerische Zusammenhänge einzuarbeiten und zur Weiterentwicklung des Kreativ-Teams beizutragen


Dein Profil

  • Sehr starkes, designorientiertes Portfolio mit überzeugenden Branding-, Website- und Digitalprojekten

  • Erfahrung mit Logoentwicklung, Designsystemen, Brand Guidelines, Typografie, Farbsystemen und Bildwelten
  • Sehr gutes Verständnis dafür, wie eine Marke vom Logo und Grundsystem bis zur digitalen Anwendung funktioniert
  • Sehr sicherer Umgang mit Figma und sicherer Umgang mit der Adobe Creative Suite
  • Verständnis von Responsive Design und digitalen Designsystemen
  • Motion-/After-Effects-Kenntnisse von Vorteil
  • Hohe Kompetenz im Umgang mit AI und der Anwendung neuer KreativtechnologienInteresse an strategischen und inhaltlichen Fragestellungen sowie die Bereitschaft, das «Warum» hinter einer Gestaltung zu verstehen
  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und gute Englischkenntnisse beziehungsweise sichere Kommunikation im deutschsprachigen Umfeld
  • Gesucht wird keine reine Production-Designer-Persönlichkeit und kein:e reine:r Print- oder Editorial-Grafiker:in: Du musst Branding verstehen, digital denken und einen hohen gestalterischen Anspruch mitbringen


Unser Angebot

  • Spannende Projekte für nationale und internationale Kunden an der Schnittstelle von Strategie, Marke, Design und digitaler Transformation
  • Interdisziplinäres Team mit flachen Hierarchien, offener Kommunikation und direktem Austausch mit der Unternehmensführung
  • Möglichkeit, die nächste Phase der Hotz Group aktiv mitzugestalten und den Ausbau unseres Kreativ-Teams nachhaltig zu prägen
  • Zusammenarbeit mit Strateg:innen, Berater:innen und Spezialist:innen aus dem Brand Leadership Circle
  • Moderner Arbeitsplatz in Steinhausen/Zug mit sehr guter Autobahn- und ÖV-Anbindung
  • Regelmässige Firmenevents, kostenfreie Getränke, Kaffee und frisches Obst sowie Zuschuss zum Mittagessen
  • 29 Tage Ferien sowie attraktive Mitarbeitervorteile und Vergünstigungen – weil uns Erholung, Work-Life-Balance und dein Wohl am Herzen liegen

raw.title: Senior Backend Developer (Go) — Full Remote, European Timezones Only (UTC−1 to UTC+3)
raw.description:
Read this first — two non-negotiables

  1. Go is the job, not a bonus skill. We're only considering candidates with 5+ years of hands-on, production experience in Go. If Go isn't (one of) your primary languages, this role won't be a match — and we'd rather save you the time.

  2. You must live in a European timezone (UTC−1 to UTC+3). This is a hard requirement. Applications from outside this range won't be considered, regardless of how strong the profile is.

Still with us? Great — here's why this role is worth your attention.

Who we are

We're Jobtome (https://weare.jobtome.com/) — an HR Tech company building the modern web applications that companies use to run complex hiring and recruitment workflows at scale.

Our products are highly interactive, data-driven, and built for real-world usage — not demos. We work with a strong product mindset, short feedback loops, and a pragmatic engineering culture: quality, ownership, and code we're still proud of a year from now.

The role

You'll join our engineering team as a Senior Go Backend Developer and take real ownership of critical backend systems and services — not ticket-pushing, actual ownership.

You'll design, build, and evolve the backend services that power our products, weigh in on architectural decisions, improve system reliability, and help shape how backend engineering is done across the company.

This is a hands-on senior role: you'll write production Go every day and be deeply involved in technical decisions that have real impact.


Quick reminder before the details

5+ years of production Go experience — required Based in a European timezone (UTC−1 to UTC+3)

What you'll do

  • Design, build, and maintain backend services written in Go

  • Build and evolve APIs (GraphQL and/or REST) behind complex product workflows

  • Design scalable, reliable, and maintainable backend architectures

  • Work closely with frontend engineers, product managers, data engineers, and designers

  • Contribute to data modeling, business logic, and performance optimization

  • Review code and take part in architectural and technical discussions

  • Raise the bar on code quality, testing, observability, and system resilience

  • Actively tackle refactoring, technical debt, and long-term improvements

  • Own backend features end to end, from design to production

  • Take part in Agile ceremonies (planning, stand-ups, retrospectives)

Our stack

Go sits at the center of everything. Around it, you'll work with (and should be comfortable with):

  • API design (GraphQL and/or REST)

  • PostgreSQL (or similar relational databases)

  • BigQuery and other NoSQL databases

  • Distributed systems and service-oriented architectures

  • Docker and CI/CD pipelines (GitLab pipelines preferred)

  • A cloud-infrastructure mindset (GCP or other providers)

  • Observability tools (logging, metrics, tracing)

  • Testing (unit and/or integration)

  • Kubernetes

Nice to have:

  • Working experience with Python

  • Exposure to Protobuf and gRPC

What "senior" means to us

Titles vary — here's what we actually mean. A senior engineer at Jobtome can:

  • Work independently without needing perfect specs

  • Own complex features and systems

  • Make informed architectural decisions and explain the trade-offs

  • Write clean, maintainable, well-structured code

  • Spot problems early and propose solutions

  • Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical people alike

  • Raise the team's quality bar through example and reviews

How we work

  • Full remote — from anywhere within UTC−1 to UTC+3 (yes, we're repeating it on purpose)

  • Core hours, with flexibility around them

  • Daily working language: English
